summary.headline: ACME Solar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR705 crore, FY26 revenue INR2,507 crore (+59%), with 2.3 GW of merchant BESS now running.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR705 crore (+31% YoY), including INR157 crore of other income, and FY26 revenue was INR2,507 crore (+59%) on capacity addition and higher CUF. PAT was INR138 crore for the quarter (19.6% margin) and INR498 crore for FY26 (19.9%), with management citing EBITDA margins above 90%. Management said about 2.3 GW of BESS is now commissioned and earning on merchant and short-term contracts at roughly INR2.2 crore per day. Management also flagged a timeline shift: most of the 1.5 GW generation commissioning and the 10 GWh BESS target depend on CTU substations, some of which are delayed by up to about 6 months.

financial_highlights.metric: Total revenue (Q4 FY26, incl. other income)
Weighted average cost of debt (operational projects)
financial_highlights.change: Refinancing cut rate by ~150 bps on INR3,300 crore

segments.name: Solar and wind generation (operational)
segments.commentary: Operational contracted generation capacity is 2,990 MW. Management said plant and grid availability were above 99% for the year, and FY26 portfolio CUF was about 26%. Sikar (Rajasthan) new plants ran at about 29-30% CUF for the year, and roughly 28%+ in Q4.

segments.name: BESS (merchant)
segments.commentary: About 2.3 GWh of BESS is commissioned, mostly in March, and earns about INR2.2 crore per day net (over INR60 crore per month) from tariff arbitrage. Round-trip efficiency is 88-90%. Management said the Q3 battery contribution was negligible.

guidance_outlook: Target of about 1.5 GW of generation projects commissioned in FY27, with the first FDRE commissioning at Neemuch substation in June 2026.

Battery target of about 10 GWh for the next calendar year: roughly 8.5 GWh merchant and 1.5 GWh in FDRE format. Management said the 10 GWh target is achievable on connectivity and financing; supply and geopolitics are the main uncertainties.
Around 2.5 GW of connectivity at operational substations (Fatehgarh-1, Fatehgarh-2 under STOA, Bikaner-3) is ready for BESS discharge at night.
Under-construction portfolio of 5.1 GW (total pipeline 8,071 MW) with PPA-signed capacity of 3,280 MW; PPA-signed projects expected to be commissioned by FY28.
Management expects a run-rate EBITDA jump as battery revenue starts; a 75-80% EBITDA margin is expected on merchant BESS at INR6 tariff arbitrage.
capex_capacity: Committed total capex INR12,475 crore: INR6,445 crore incurred in FY26 and INR6,030 crore in purchase orders. Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in Q4.
Gross block rose about INR3,460 crore in FY26, of which about INR1,000-1,100 crore is battery.

Capital advances of about INR323 crore, mainly battery (10% advance against bank guarantee) and turbines (20% advance). Management said solar module capex is being deferred until the LTA is operational.
Under-construction portfolio added 301 MW of peak-power FDRE with SECI in the quarter; total under construction is 5.1 GW, requiring about 17 GWh of BESS.

Commissioning timeline: NTPC hybrid solar ready, LTA by December 2026; Pachora wind component a couple of quarters later; SJVN Fatehgarh full FDRE by FY27 end (LTA March 2027). Pavagada and Anantapur are targeted this year per CTU timelines.
demand_pricing: India peak demand hit 256 GW on 25 April 2026, against 250 GW in May 2024. Electricity consumption grew 8.9% in April 2026.

India added about 55 GW of RE in FY26 (cumulative 283 GW). Management expects peak-power and FDRE/BESS-linked bids to dominate, with 15-20 GW of bids this year (fewer than last year) and state plus central tenders of 20-30 GW.

Management said peak-power products sell fastest, followed by partial peak, then wind; plain solar sells slowest. Thermal-equivalent BESS pricing is cited at INR9-10 per unit at peak, with the annual realisation at INR7-8.
Receivable days have fallen to about 14-15 days from about 180 days in the past. Trade receivables fell 13% YoY. Central offtakers take a cash discount and pay in about 10 days.

qa_highlights.question: What battery capex was incurred and how much BESS capacity was commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery capex was about INR1,000-1,200 crore in the last quarter, and about 1.3 GWh was commissioned as of the prior quarter. Battery capacity reached 2.3 GWh by the time of the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the run-rate EBITDA from existing capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 EBITDA including other income was about INR2,200 crore, mainly from the PPA projects. BESS revenue at INR2.2 crore per day is over INR60 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is there curtailment, and how is future project allocation shaped?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 2 projects are connected to the state grid. FY26 curtailment impact was INR5-6 crore, plus INR3 crore of STU impact in Rajasthan. Nearly all of the portfolio is on CTU, with the goal that each project has a battery.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross block growing faster than run-rate EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR1,000-1,100 crore of the gross block increase is battery, and the battery was commissioned late in the year, so it is not yet in run-rate EBITDA. Wind is also still ramping in phases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from LOA conversion and CERC connectivity rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 6.2 GW of signed PPAs are under construction, and 3.2 GW of LOA has converted to PPA. Management does not expect LOAs to be surrendered, and it has a backup plan of using connectivity for future bids or battery-linked projects.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the BESS arbitrage last?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duration is uncertain. It estimated the national need at about 200-300 GWh, and said the peak price should stay at INR7-8 for four to five years given gas constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Are CTU substation delays affecting commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 60% of substations are on time and the maximum delay is typically 6 months. Where delays are known, modules are deferred, and no penalty applies under the sync-up framework.

risks_watch: Commissioning timelines depend on CTU substations and LTA dates; management cites delays of up to about 6 months, with the 1.5 GW FY27 target at risk.
BESS merchant revenue depends on the peak-offpeak price spread; management concedes the duration is uncertain and the spread could narrow as more batteries come online.
The 10 GWh battery target depends on supply of material and geopolitical factors.
CERC draft proposal on LOA-based connectivity and PPA signing risk for about 850 MW of older PPAs still in discussion.
Q4 PLF fell about 1% YoY, which management attributed to lower irradiation and curtailment.
Management commentary on the new CFO is that Arun Chopra has replaced Rajat Kumar Singh; watch for continuity.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed on BESS deployment, regulatory tailwinds and the timeline. Management was less specific on Q4 battery EBITDA, asset-level margins and the reason for the gross block to EBITDA gap, deferring to later updates.

growth.why: Management targets 1.5 GW generation and about 10 GWh BESS in FY27 with 2.5 GW of substation connectivity ready for BESS, but CTU substation delays of up to about 6 months and solar capex deferral add timing risk; Q4 revenue rose 31% YoY with FY26 revenue up 59%, and no explicit FY27 revenue growth % was given.
